CampaignPolicy.description:
Budgets and limits for one campaign.

Production rules need the target's environment, which is not part of the
policy, so a bare ``CampaignPolicy`` does NOT enforce them. Campaign
creation must validate through :class:`CampaignRequest`, which always does.
The context form (``context={"environment": ...}``) and
:func:`validate_policy_for_target` exist for callers that already hold
both halves. Violations are rejected, never clamped.
CampaignPolicy.title: CampaignPolicy

consensus table.

TargetUpdate.description:
Partial update. ``environment`` cannot change (create a new target instead).

``auth``: give the full object; secret fields left out keep their stored
value when the auth ``type`` is unchanged. Changing the endpoint, the auth
type or URLs, or ``allowed_auth_hosts`` clears verification.
``oncall_webhook_url: null`` removes the webhook.

post.description:
Set the global DB kill switch (platform admins only: ``CANARY_PLATFORM_ADMINS``).
It halts every org's campaigns, so an org admin cannot flip it. The env var CANARY_KILL_SWITCH is independent.
Create a CI key for yourself (it acts with your role). Browser sessions only.

get.description:
WP10 differential gate of this (candidate) campaign against ``baseline``.

Pure read: nothing is launched or stored. Both campaigns must be in the
caller's org (404 otherwise). Default gate policy.

SSE stream of campaign events. ``Last-Event-ID`` replays events with a larger ``seq``.

Events come from the persisted log, so a disconnect only ends this
generator; the run (in a worker process) is unaffected.

put.description:
Move a finding along its lifecycle; the reviewer is the caller. 409 on an
illegal transition; closing statuses need a rationale (422).

post.description:
Register an (unverified) target in the caller's org.

The plaintext verification token is returned in this response only; just its
hash is kept.

delete.description:
Delete a target. One with campaign history is archived instead (hidden from
the org, unverified, credentials dropped). 409 while a campaign is active.

schema.title: Response Delete Target Api V2 Targets  Target Id  Delete

post.description:
Send one fixed benign message ("Hello") to the target and report what came back.

Allowed before verification (it is how an operator checks the wizard settings),
so it sends exactly one constant, harmless request and nothing user-supplied.
The endpoint and auth URLs pass the SSRF guard first. The reply is redacted and
the target's own credentials are masked. Credentials are never returned.
Run one ownership check. 200 either way; ``verified`` carries the outcome.
